changelog: First release: every SF IR op of Stage 3 and every public Python function.
global_rules: Static shapes. Every value has a static shape of rank <= 3. No dynamic shapes.
Lockstep. A program (block) is one vector of lanes. Control flow is if-converted: `if` on a lane value becomes a predicate carried on each op (`pred=`).
Ops with a predicate: values on dead lanes are don't-care, but events and memory effects must be masked.
Events never change the bits. The policy (raise / warn / ignore) is applied by the host after the launch from the event counts.
Arithmetic truncates toward zero; only narrow rounds (half to even). Add/sub/sum saturate; mul underflows; div overflows when |a| >= |b|.
No reassociation of add, sum, or the k loop of dot. No distributivity. No float math anywhere: lower on integer codes.
Faults (out of bounds, integer division by zero) abort the launch with SFDeviceError and leave buffers undefined.

Host pre-flight: before a launch the host decides everything it can (a zero divisor, an op that must saturate everywhere, an op that cannot saturate). The compiler never needs to handle those cases specially, but must still produce correct bits for them.
Width: sfN for N < 16 runs on the sf16 datapath shifted left by 16-N and must be re-truncated (low bits masked) after every op so the result equals true sfN.

types.sfN: Superfloat code, N in 4..16. Stored as a signed integer k in [-M, M], M = 2^(N-1) - 1. Value = k / 2^(N-1). Sign-magnitude on the chip; the IR carries k as a plain signed integer. There is no code -2^(N-1), no NaN, no infinity.
types.int: 64-bit signed integer (indices, offsets, loop math). Never overflows in practice; the reference uses int64 and does not wrap-check.
types.ptr<sfN>: Base address of a global buffer of sfN codes. Only appears as a kernel parameter; address arithmetic is `ptr + int offsets` and is folded into load/store.

events.overflow: the exact result did not fit; the result is saturated to +-M (sign of the exact result).
events.underflow: the exact result was nonzero but the stored result is 0.
events.divide: division by a zero code. Result is +-M with the sign of the dividend (0 if dividend is 0).
events.invalid: no real answer (sqrt of a negative). Result is 0.

predication.pure: No side effects. Under a predicate the op may run on every lane; masked lanes produce values that are never observed. Safe to speculate.
predication.events: Value is pure, but events are only counted on live lanes (lanes where the predicate in force is true). Lowering may compute every lane but MUST mask the event flags with the predicate, or it will report events from dead lanes.
predication.memory: Only live lanes (mask AND predicate) touch memory. Masked lanes must not read, write or fault.

ops.name: param
ops.result: int or sfN scalar for kind int/sf; none for ptr (the buffer is bound by value id)
ops.semantics: Reads a scalar kernel argument. Pointer params produce no value; loads and stores refer to them directly.

ops.name: const
ops.result: int, sfN or bool, filled to the result shape
ops.semantics: A literal. For sf the value is already a code (quantized at trace time with round half to even, through the policy).

ops.name: program_id
ops.semantics: Index of this program (block) in the launch grid on that axis.

ops.name: thread_idx
ops.shape: block_dim laid out on the used axes (rank = highest axis with block_dim > 1)
ops.semantics: Lane index along axis. @sf.kernel only. The IR is lockstep: the whole block is one vector.
ops.hw_v1: lane id (8 threads per tile in v1)

ops.name: arange
ops.semantics: start, start+1, ..., end-1.

ops.name: broadcast
ops.shape: attr shape (numpy broadcast rules from x.shape)
ops.semantics: Repeat x to the target shape. No numeric change.

ops.name: reshape
ops.semantics: Row-major reshape. No numeric change.

ops.name: transpose
ops.semantics: 2-D transpose.

ops.name: iadd
ops.semantics: a + b
rewrites: ordinary integer algebra is legal (no saturation)

ops.name: isub
ops.semantics: a - b
rewrites: ordinary integer algebra is legal (no saturation)

ops.name: imul
ops.semantics: a * b
rewrites: ordinary integer algebra is legal (no saturation)

ops.name: idiv
ops.semantics: FLOOR division (Python //), not truncation: -7 // 2 = -4.
faults: any lane with b == 0 faults the whole launch (SFDeviceError)
notes: the zero check covers every lane of the broadcast, live or not

ops.name: imod
ops.semantics: Python modulo: result has the sign of b. -7 % 2 = 1.
faults: b == 0 in any lane faults the launch

ops.name: ineg
ops.semantics: -a

ops.name: icmp

attrs.op: lt | le | gt | ge | eq | ne

ops.semantics: Integer compare.

ops.name: bool_to_int
ops.semantics: false -> 0, true -> 1
python: using a mask in int math

ops.name: and
ops.semantics: a AND b. Also emitted to combine nested predicates.

ops.name: or
ops.semantics: a OR b

ops.name: xor
ops.semantics: a XOR b

ops.name: not
ops.semantics: NOT a

ops.name: where
ops.semantics: x where c else y, per lane. Exact, no events.

ops.name: add
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: s = a + b (exact integer). If |s| > M: result = sign(s)*M, overflow. Else result = s.
rewrites: commutative: a+b = b+a (legal)
NOT associative: (a+b)+c != a+(b+c) when an intermediate saturates. Do not reassociate, do not reorder a chain, do not tree-reduce.
x + 0 -> x (legal)
never turn a+a into 2*a via mul (mul cannot represent 2)
notes: sfN < 16 on the sf16 datapath: shift left by 16-N, add, saturate at the sfN max shifted, shift back. The saturation threshold must be sfN's M, not sf16's.

ops.name: sub
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: s = a - b; saturate like add.
rewrites: a - b -> a + neg(b) is legal (neg is exact since the range is symmetric)
NOT associative: (a+b)+c != a+(b+c) when an intermediate saturates. Do not reassociate, do not reorder a chain, do not tree-reduce.

ops.name: mul
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: p = a * b (exact, up to 2(N-1)+1 bits). result = trunc_toward_zero(p / 2^(N-1)). underflow if p != 0 and result == 0. |result| < M always, so mul never overflows.
rewrites: commutative (legal)
NOT associative: truncation after each product
NOT distributive over add
x * 0 -> 0 (legal, no event)
there is no 1.0, so there is no multiplicative identity to fold
notes: truncation is toward zero, NOT floor: an arithmetic right shift on a negative product is wrong. Shift the magnitude, then reapply the sign.

ops.name: div
ops.shape: numpy broadcast of the operand shapes (rank <= 3); scalars are shape ()
ops.semantics: b == 0: divide event, result = sign(a)*M (0 if a == 0). |a| >= |b|: overflow, result = sign(a)*sign(b)*M. Else result = trunc_toward_zero(a * 2^(N-1) / b).
ops.hw_v1: NOT SUPPORTED on v1 (no divider). Device.supported_ops excludes it; the runtime raises SFUnsupportedError. Host pre-flight decides every b == 0 lane before launch.
rewrites: no rewrites; in particular a/b is not a * (1/b) (1/b always overflows)
notes: the event check order is divide first, then overflow; a lane with b == 0 reports divide only
sf.div(where=mask) lowers to a predicated div: masked lanes give 0 and no event

ops.name: fma
ops.semantics: t = mul(a, b) (truncated, may underflow); result = add(t, c) (may saturate). Bit-identical to add(mul(a, b), c). This is NOT a fused single-rounding fma.
rewrites: add(mul(a,b),c) <-> fma(a,b,c) is legal both ways (same bits)
commutative in a and b
notes: on v4.8.1 hardware (wide accumulator, single rounding) this would change: major version bump

ops.name: neg
ops.semantics: -a. Exact (range is symmetric), no events.
rewrites: neg(neg(x)) -> x

ops.name: abs
ops.semantics: |a|. Exact, no events.

ops.name: sqrt
ops.semantics: a < 0: invalid, result 0. Else result = isqrt(a * 2^(N-1)) (floor of the exact root). Never overflows.
ops.hw_v1: NOT SUPPORTED on v1 (no sqrt unit); runtime raises SFUnsupportedError

ops.name: widen
ops.semantics: result = a << (M - N). Exact, no events.

ops.name: narrow
ops.semantics: q = round_half_to_even(a / 2^(N-M)) (floor divmod, then round up if remainder > half, or == half and q odd). If |q| > M_max: overflow, clip to +-M_max. underflow if a != 0 and result == 0.
notes: this is the ONLY op that rounds to nearest. All arithmetic truncates toward zero.

ops.name: cmp

attrs.op: lt | le | gt | ge | eq | ne

ops.semantics: Integer compare of the codes (exact).

ops.name: cmp_lit

attrs.op: lt | le | gt | ge | eq | ne
attrs.value: int code threshold, decided at trace time

ops.semantics: Compare against a Python literal that may not be representable (e.g. x < 1). The tracer turns the exact literal into an equivalent integer threshold, so the op is a plain integer compare.

ops.name: maximum
ops.semantics: max of codes. Exact.
rewrites: associative and commutative (legal to reorder)

ops.name: minimum
ops.semantics: min of codes. Exact.
rewrites: associative and commutative

ops.name: sum
ops.shape: x.shape with axis removed (() for None)
ops.semantics: acc = 0; for i = 0 .. n-1 in index order: acc = add(acc, x[i]) (saturating each step). Overflow if any step saturated. Saturation is sticky in the sense that later steps continue from +-M.
rewrites: NOT associative: (a+b)+c != a+(b+c) when an intermediate saturates. Do not reassociate, do not reorder a chain, do not tree-reduce.
result DEPENDS on order: [M, 1, -1] gives M-1, [1, -1, M] gives M

ops.name: max
ops.semantics: max along axis. Exact.
rewrites: any order / tree is legal

ops.name: min
ops.semantics: min along axis. Exact.
rewrites: any order / tree is legal

ops.name: dot
ops.semantics: For each (i, j): acc = 0; for t = 0 .. k-1: acc = fma(a[i,t], b[t,j], acc). Every product truncated, every add saturated, at width N, in increasing t.
rewrites: k must be accumulated in increasing order. Tiling over m and n is free; tiling over k is legal ONLY if the partial sum of tile 1 is fed as the initial acc of tile 2 (no separate partials added later)
split-k, tree reduction, and wider accumulators are NOT legal
notes: addmm(c, a, b) = acc starts at c, not 0, then the same chain

ops.name: load
ops.semantics: live = mask AND predicate. Live lanes: ptr[offs]. Others: other. Offsets are element indices, not bytes.
ops.memory: READ global buffer ptr at offs on live lanes only
faults: any live lane with offs < 0 or offs >= buffer size faults the launch. Masked lanes never fault.

ops.name: store
ops.semantics: live = mask AND predicate. ptr[offs] = val on live lanes. If two live lanes hit the same offset, the reference keeps the last lane in row-major order; kernels should not rely on this.
ops.memory: WRITE global buffer ptr at offs on live lanes only
faults: a live lane out of bounds faults the launch. Earlier writes are NOT rolled back: after a fault the buffers are undefined.
notes: two programs writing the same address is a race; the result is undefined (the simulator runs programs in order)

ops.name: shared_load

attrs.buf: shared buffer id (declared on the kernel)

ops.semantics: Live lanes read shared[buf][idx]; masked lanes give 0.
faults: live lane out of bounds faults

ops.name: shared_store
ops.semantics: Live lanes write shared[buf][idx] = val.
ops.memory: WRITE block-local shared buffer. Shared memory is zeroed at the start of every program.
faults: live lane out of bounds faults

ops.name: barrier
ops.semantics: All lanes of the block reach this point before any continues. In lockstep IR this orders shared-memory accesses; nothing may be moved across it.
notes: must not be placed under a divergent predicate
